description:
FOUND s505 (Fable, 2026-10-03) by a review probe of s501t (#155 tie): core Tie::File now ties and reads correctly, but `$l[1] = "CHANGED"` writes the record WITHOUT its record separator -- the file reads `l1|CHANGEDl3|l4` where perl writes `l1|CHANGED|l3|l4`.  Silent corruption of a file on disk.

CAUSE (probed perl -> main a33ce274 -> a0899ba6; identical on both PCL trees, so PRE-EXISTING and not tie): Tie::File::STORE does `my ($self, $n, $rec) = @_; $self->_fixrecs($rec);` and _fixrecs appends the separator THROUGH @_ (`my $self = shift; for (@_) { $_ .= $self->{recsep} unless ... }`).  A plain `my` lexical of a SUB passed to a callee the compiler cannot see -- a METHOD call, a package-QUALIFIED call (`T::m2($self, $rec)`), a dynamic method, a coderef call -- is passed as a COPY, so the write is lost.  That is the documented partial in docs/not-supported.md "@_ argument aliasing -- PARTIAL" (what still COPIES: coderef calls, method dispatch, cross-file callees).

TWO THINGS THAT ENTRY DOES NOT SAY:
(1) THE BACKSTOP IS SILENT HERE.  The entry promises the runtime warning "Cannot modify non-boxed value" as the loud backstop "for exactly these".  ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s505/review/min/f4c.pl prints NOTHING on stderr while seven of its ten rows are wrong (`$_ .= "x"` in a foreach over @_, `$_[1] .= "x"`): the callee receives a fresh BOX holding the copy, so the write succeeds -- into the copy.  The warning only fires for a RAW value.  So this is a silent wrong, not an announced one.
(2) A QUALIFIED call to a sub IN THE SAME FILE (`T::m2($self, $rec)`) copies too, although the callee body is visible -- writes_args is consulted by bare name only.

Reproducers: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s505/review/min/f4.pl, f4b.pl (which callee shapes: only the parameter-of-a-sub + unseen-callee combination fails; a FILE-level `my` is right, an ARRAY parameter is right, a parameter that is also read by another statement form (`chomp(my $c = $rec)`) is right), f4c.pl (ten caller shapes; perl: all `vx`), and the module row: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s505/review/r501t-mods.pl row 13.

WHAT TO MEASURE BEFORE DESIGNING (this is the E2c / #189 / #862 territory -- read DECIDED for writes_args first): how many call sites in the corpus pass a raw-slot `my` scalar to a method / qualified / coderef call (one counter in VarAnnotator at the arg-to-writer decision), and what boxing ALL of them costs on tools/bench-exec.pl rows methret / sigarith / passarr.  Cheaper candidates, in order: (a) resolve a package-QUALIFIED same-file callee through the existing writes_args fact (finding 2 -- no cost); (b) a file-level fact "some sub in this compilation unit writes @_ and is reachable as a method" boxing only arguments of method calls whose NAME matches such a sub (same-file methods; Tie::File is one file); (c) cross-file: the fact rides the module cache manifest.  The USER rule applies: a correctness fix that slows the generated code is flagged with its number.

Until fixed: add Tie::File to the not-supported entry affected list (real module, silent file corruption), and say there that the backstop does not fire for these shapes.
subject: A sub parameter (`my` scalar) passed to a METHOD / qualified / coderef call is COPIED, so the callee`s write through @_ is lost SILENTLY (the documented @_-aliasing partial; its "loud backstop" does not fire): core Tie::File STORE drops the record separator -- `$l[1] = "x"` corrupts the file
